issues.description: Field ExcellenceLand.excellencyLevel: The UML in the problem statement declares the attribute 'excellencyLevel' as type double (problem_statement.md line 35). The solution implementation (src/de/tum/in/ase/ExcellenceLand.java) declares the field as type int, and the constructor and getter use int. This mismatch between 'double' in the UML and 'int' in the implementation will confuse students about the correct attribute type and the expected constructor/getter signatures and can cause tests or expected constructor signatures to fail.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the implementation match the UML by changing the type of ExcellenceLand.excellencyLevel from int to double in the field, constructor parameter, and getter. Concretely: declare 'private double excellencyLevel;', change the constructor signature to 'public ExcellenceLand(double excellencyLevel, boolean excellentEnough, List<Ride> rides)', assign the double parameter to the field, and change 'public int getExcellencyLevel()' to 'public double getExcellencyLevel()'. Adjust any downstream code or tests accordingly.
